text.title: Ads Budget Optimization Failure Modes
text.summary: 8 antipatterns observed in real deployments of Ads Budget Optimization — premature cut, single-step doubling, no test reserve, equal distribution, one-step doubling, test budget eliminated under pressure, 3-4 day cuts, CPA without downstream quality. Each pairs symptom + sourced root-cause + concrete fix.

section.title: Antipatterns

antipattern.symptom: Campaign cut on day 2 due to high CPA; identical campaign re-launched day 8 wins.
antipattern.fix: Hold all cuts until day 7 OR sample-size; document early-signal as 'noise' in ops log.

antipattern.symptom: Winning campaign budget doubled; smart bidding collapses for 7 days; CPA spikes.
antipattern.fix: Cap weekly step at 20%; ramp over 3-4 weeks for doubling target.

antipattern.symptom: 100% budget in scaling winners; 6 months later all creatives fatigued; CTR collapses across account.
antipattern.fix: Reinstate 10% test reserve; commit to >=1 test per cycle.

section.p: Common budget allocation mistakes and their fixes.

antipattern.symptom: Equal budget distribution across all campaigns regardless of performance.
antipattern.root-cause: Ignores efficiency variance; funds losing campaigns at the same rate as winning ones, capping overall ROAS.
antipattern.fix: Partition 70/20/10 by efficiency ratio (never-collapse-test-budget rule); rebalance monthly on the reallocation decision matrix.

antipattern.symptom: Doubling a campaign budget in one step when performance looks good.
antipattern.root-cause: Triggers learning phase reset; CPA spikes 20-80% for 3-7 days, erasing the efficiency gains that prompted the increase.
antipattern.fix: Cap each increase at 30% and wait 3-5 days between steps (scaling-increment-30-percent rule).

antipattern.symptom: Eliminating the testing budget during periods of pressure to hit efficiency targets.
antipattern.root-cause: Destroys the innovation pipeline; proven campaigns eventually plateau, and without tests there are no future winners to scale.
antipattern.fix: Hold the 10% test reserve as a fixed line; take efficiency pressure out of the 20% optimizing tranche instead.

antipattern.symptom: Cutting a campaign after 3-4 days of poor performance.
antipattern.root-cause: Insufficient data; platform algorithms need 7-14 days minimum and 50+ conversions before performance stabilizes — early data is high-variance noise.
antipattern.fix: Hold cuts until 7 days or the sample-size threshold (premature-cut-block rule) and keep the campaign above its learning threshold for 2 weeks (min-learning-threshold-two-weeks rule).

antipattern.symptom: Optimizing CPA without tracking downstream quality (lead-to-close rate, LTV).
antipattern.root-cause: A $20 CPA from a channel that produces 2% close rates is worse than a $100 CPA from a channel with 20% close rates — cost-per-customer matters, not cost-per-lead.
antipattern.fix: Derive target CPA from LTV (target-cpa-from-ltv rule) and compare channels on efficiency ratio with close rate folded in (cross-channel-by-efficiency-ratio rule).
